The points strictly inside satisfy $-5 < x < 5$ and $-4 < y < 4$.

- $x$ can be any of $-4, \dots, 4$, which gives 9 values.
- $y$ can be any of $-3, \dots, 3$, which gives 7 values.
- So there are $9 \times 7 = 63$ interior points.

Solution 2 is correct.

Solution 1 makes two errors. It subtracts only the boundary of the smaller rectangle from the 143 points of the larger one. It never removes the outer ring of points. Its boundary count of 34 is also not the true number of boundary points.

Solution 3 counts only the points in the open quadrants. It leaves out the interior points that lie on the axes:
- 7 points on the y-axis with $x=0$.
- 9 points on the x-axis with $y=0$.
- The origin is in both sets, so the axes add $7 + 9 - 1 = 15$ points.

Adding these gives $48 + 15 = 63$, which agrees with Solution 2.

CHOICE: 2
